relationship: Prime-factor copy counts determine HCF through shared minimum counts and LCM through combined maximum counts.

learnerLoop.action: Build prime-factor rows, pair matching copies and compare their counts.
learnerLoop.modelChange: Pairs and remaining prime copies are classified for HCF and LCM.
learnerLoop.evidence: Factor rows, pair markers and count summaries reveal the two products.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Pair another common prime or certify that no pair remains.

invariants: Only identical prime copies can form a common pair.
HCF uses minimum exponents and LCM uses maximum exponents.
safeAdaptations: Use other composite-number pairs with visible prime-copy accounting.
Vary working support without hiding the minimum-versus-maximum comparison.
nonGoals: Finding HCF or LCM from unstructured factor lists without prime multiplicities.

task.description: Current problem statement and supplied quantities.
task.visibility: Shown at the start of each problem or stage.

model.description: Operated construction and its live measurements; see quantities for what is given and revealed.
model.visibility: Present for the current problem; child controls and readouts follow the states described below.

working.description: Ordered calculations, learner entries and consequential evidence for the current task.
working.visibility: Present for the current problem; child controls and readouts follow the states described below.

completion.description: Achievement, next task or learning transition.
completion.visibility: Shown only when the local completion conditions below are satisfied; representation controls are separately identified.

confirmation.description: Confirm that no additional common prime pair remains.
confirmation.visibility: Present for the current problem; child controls and readouts follow the states described below.

copy-evidence.description: Copies required to build the common multiple.
copy-evidence.visibility: Updated from the completed decomposition/pairing state.

integer-pair.description: Two positive integers and their prime-factor multisets. Repeated equal primes are multiplicities, not separate unknown variables.
integer-pair.source: Numbers are given; decompositions are supplied or built according to Working level.
integer-pair.output: Factor products and divisibility feedback appear immediately.

shared-pairs.description: A matching of equal prime copies across the two rows.
shared-pairs.domain: Discrete token pairs, with each token usable once.
shared-pairs.output: The lanes and HCF/LCM factor products update as pairs form.

hcf-and-lcm.source: Products follow the paired/unpaired factor structure; entered only in Some/All.
hcf-and-lcm.output: Product fields unlock after the shared-factor claim is confirmed.

modes.none: Both prime decompositions are supplied; learner still pairs shared factors and confirms no pair remains. HCF/LCM products are shown.
modes.some: One decomposition (chosen by seed parity) must be built, then HCF and LCM entered.
modes.all: Both decompositions must be built, then HCF and LCM entered.

dependencies: Each built factor product must equal its given integer before pairing.
Factor editing locks once pairing begins.
Confirmation is valid only when no equal-prime pairing remains; required product answers then finish the problem.
implementation.completion: finalised() requires rowsReady(), no possiblePrimes(), session.confirmed and, for Some/All, both product answers exactly correct.
